text:
Harry Kane injured as Bayern Munich and PSG face injury crises plus Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe miss penalties
Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal missed penalties but still won, while Harry Kane was injured and didn't. Adam Bate picks out the big stories from the continent in the Euro Debrief, a Sky Sports column focusing on the major European leagues and more...
Monday 23 November 2026 09:04, UK
Welcome to The Euro Debrief, the Sky Sports column in which Adam Bate rounds up some of the key stories from the latest matches across the continent. This week:
- Are Bayern in crisis?
- Superstar penalty misses
- Malen magic as Inter slip
- Injury problems for PSG
- Title twist in Norway
Bundesliga: Crisis for Bayern?
Can a club be in crisis when they are unbeaten in all competitions? Probably not. But all is not well at Bayern Munich. They are off the top spot in the Bundesliga and currently outside the top eight in the Champions League. But the problems for Bayern are off the field.
Harry Kane's injury in the 1-1 draw at home to Cologne on Friday night will see him miss at least three months of action. Michael Olise's injury in the same game was less serious but adds to the issues with Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari all out already.
Ordinarily, that would see Bayern lean heavily on Jamal Musiala but that is a little awkward. The player's neurological concerns that led him to collapse twice during pre-season sparked unseemly comments from senior Bayern luminaries about his future.
Honorary president Uli Hoeness and club legend Karl-Heinz Rummenigge appeared to suggest a contract renegotiation would be appropriate given their view that Musiala can no longer perform his job to the same level. Even players' union FIFPRO intervened.

The expectation is that Bayern will look to strengthen their forward line in January but there are four otherwise winnable games to play in the Bundesliga before then. Any slip could let Borussia Dortmund pull further clear because Niko Kovac's team look relentless.
Once again, they were functional rather than fantastic in beating bottom-club Borussia Monchengladbach but their form is built on solid foundations. Their six clean sheets so far are three times the number of Bayern. Keep that up and the opportunity is there.
On the subject of keeping things going, no surprise to see two veterans among the goals elsewhere. Patrik Schick scored again in Bayer Leverkusen's 4-0 win over Paderborn, while Niclas Fullkrug netted late as Werder Bremen beat Hamburg by the same score.
The two men top the Bundesliga scoring charts with Schick, the baby at 30, one goal behind the 33-year-old Fullkrug who is now into double figures. Still on loan from West Ham, it means that Fullkrug has now scored as many goals as Kane and Olise put together.
Bundesliga results: Bayern Munich 1-1 Cologne, Bayer Leverkusen 4-0 Paderborn, Borussia Monchengladbach 0-1 Borussia Dortmund, Eintracht Frankfurt 1-0 Hoffenheim, Elversberg 0-1 Freiburg, Union Berlin 1-5 RB Leipzig, Schalke 0-0 Stuttgart, Augsburg 3-1 Mainz, Werder Bremen 4-0 Hamburg.
LaLiga: Penalty woe for superstars
There is nothing unusual about Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal being in competition but usually that means scoring goals, not missing penalties. The Barcelona teenager tried to outdo his Madrid counterpart with an even worse miss from the spot this weekend.
Fortunately for the pair, neither blunder proved costly as both their teams came from behind to win at home. Real Madrid made hard work of Celta Vigo after an abysmal first half at the Bernabeu but Jude Bellingham levelled and Carlos Espi was the hero again.
The 21-year-old striker signed from Levante in the summer has now scored three goals for Madrid in LaLiga - and all of them have been late winners. In fact, this was the earliest of them so far, coming in the 85th minute. Mbappe spooning his spot-kick did not matter.
- LaLiga: Table | Fixtures & results
Lamine Yamal, meanwhile, scuffed his effort wide of the post in windy conditions at Camp Nou with his team two down to Villarreal. But he was instrumental in turning the game around for Barcelona to maintain their three-point advantage at the top of LaLiga.
The winger set up Fermin Lopez, who himself had been culpable for Villarreal's opener, before a clever flick opened up the space for the winner. Barca have conceded more goals than bottom-half teams Espanyol and Celta this season but have scored 51 times already.
Elsewhere in Spain, Atletico had the most comfortable win among the big three despite having the trickiest fixture on paper as they made the short trip to Getafe and won by three. But the biggest game of the weekend came in Seville where it was El Gran Derbi.
There was real drama too. Real Betis were leading into stoppage-time through Antony's deflected effort but centre-back Kike Salas scored an equaliser that while deserved on the balance of play - Sevilla had 25 shots to Betis' six - was a little controversial.
Salas was fortunate still to be on the pitch, with a foul that he committed while on a yellow card sparking such frustration on the Betis bench that three bookings were issued. Typical that it was his strike that somehow beat Alvaro Valles to spark wild celebrations.
LaLiga results: Athletic Club 0-1 Espanyol, Alaves 3-1 Deportivo A Coruna, Rayo Vallecano 0-1 Valencia, Sevilla 1-1 Real Betis, Real Madrid 2-1 Celta Vigo, Barcelona 3-2 Villarreal, Racing Santander 3-2 Real Sociedad, Osasuna 1-0 Malaga, Getafe 0-3 Atletico Madrid.
Serie A: Malen magic while Inter slip
Inter have been the comeback kings so often in Serie A this season that there could have been little hope of Atalanta salvaging anything when 4-2 down with 10 minutes remaining. But Franck Kessie, once of their great rivals Milan, scored a 91st-minute penalty to level it.
It was an unfortunate handball that brought it but this was a thrilling game in which English winger Jonathan Rowe set up Atalanta's third goal and Charles De Ketelaere's second, while Inter forward Francesco Pio Esposito scored his first career hat-trick.
- Serie A: Table | Fixtures & results
What is going on in Serie A? For years, Serie A had the lowest goals-per-game average of any major league and while the old cliches about Italian football have been inaccurate for a while, the current average of 3.16 goals per game is the highest in 76 years.
Four-goal home wins for Juventus and Milan helped those stats but one man beat the average on his own. Donyell Malen bagged four himself in Roma's 5-1 win at Parma as the Giallorossi leapfrogged Inter into second spot. Malen has become a phenomenon.
All four of his goals showcased the fact that he has become a genuine goal poacher but the first was beyond brilliant, the speed of his turn just unstoppable. Malen has now scored 26 league goals in 2026. Five more than anyone else in a major European league.
Twenty-five years on from Roma's last title win, hope is growing. How ironic it would be if they were denied not by Inter but by rivals Lazio who have had an even longer wait to reclaim the crown. Gennaro Gattuso's side beat Lecce to march on at the top of the table.
Both Lazio and Roma remain unbeaten after 12 games and the meeting between the two teams in the Stadio Olimpico next month now looms large. Speaking as someone who is heading to the Eternal City for that one, it now looks a mouthwatering prospect.
Serie A results: Como 2-0 Cagliari, Lazio 3-0 Lecce, Parma 1-5 Roma, Napoli 1-0 Torino, Juventus 4-0 Venezia, Bologna 1-1 Udinese, Sassuolo 0-2 Genoa, Milan 5-1 Frosinone, Atalanta 4-4 Inter.
Ligue 1: PSG injury issues increase
Given their financial dominance and status as the best team in Europe, sympathy for Paris Saint-Germain is not often forthcoming but Desire Doue deserves plenty of it. The forward has joined Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in suffering an anterior crucial ligament injury.
Doue is a magnificent talent. Speaking to one elite European coach recently, he regarded him as somehow still underrated. And there is time for him to bounce back. But it will not be this season and that presents a problem for PSG - and opportunities for others.
In Europe, there are more candidates for their crown than there are domestically. And Luis Enrique's side did still beat Nice 3-2 on Friday. But Paris FC, under Liam Rosenior, were 4-0 winners over Angers to remain just three points behind their city neighbours.
- Ligue 1: Table | Fixtures & results
Lyon are into the top four after Carlos Vicens marked his first game in charge with a win but he was the only new arrival to claim a victory. Vitor Matos lost at home in his first game since leaving Swansea for Strasbourg and Lens could not beat Toulouse at home.
But the most astonishing result of the weekend in Ligue 1 came at the Velodrome where Marseille were set for a sixth successive win that would have taken them up to third. Instead they conceded three late on to lose 3-2 to Le Mans. Always drama with Marseille.
Ligue 1 results: Troyes 3-1 Le Havre, Nice 2-3 PSG, Lens 1-1 Toulouse, Lille 0-1 Lyon, Monaco 1-1 Auxerre, Strasbourg 0-1 Brest, Paris FC 4-0 Angers, Lorient 1-1 Rennes, Marseille 2-3 Le Mans.
Elsewhere: Title drama in Norway
The tightest of title races in Norway took a big twist at the weekend. Reigning champions Viking had been ahead of Bodo/Glimt on goal difference with four rounds remaining but they were unable to match their title rivals' win at the weekend to slip off the pace.
Bodo/Glimt navigated a tricky trip to Molde comfortably enough with a 4-2 win but Viking, whose rise to the Champions League has been so impressive, were well beaten by Tromso. They went three down before clawing it back to 3-2 late on in the game. Not enough.
Given that Bodo/Glimt's remaining three fixtures are all against bottom-half teams, this could be the decisive moment in a title race that has been so close that just weeks ago the pair had identical records and could not even be separated on goal difference.
